Bullish thesis on Auckland Airport faces profit squeeze

Bulls argue that Auckland Airport is a high quality monopoly where the long term capital build and expanded regulated asset base will convert into higher, more predictable earnings. The latest year partly supports this. Passenger movements rose about 2% to just over 19 million, aeronautical revenue was higher, and EBITDAFI grew to $724m with normalized growth of 6%. That shows the core franchise is still pulling through cash despite heavy construction. However, underlying NPAT was flat at $309m while depreciation rose about 20% and reported profit fell due to fair value items. Free cash flow stayed negative with capex of about $1.07b and another 2 years of heavy spend flagged. The monopoly asset is clearly busy and earning, but the earnings uplift from the build is not yet visible at the bottom line.

Bearish concerns highlight margins, capex and regulation

The main bearish story is that Auckland Airport carries rich expectations while margins compress, capex stays heavy and regulation tightens. The latest numbers give that view real support. Net profit margin moved from 44.1% to 32.3% at the same time as depreciation stepped up and FY27 underlying earnings are guided to $290m to $330m, which brackets flat to lower profit. Capex guidance of $1.0b to $1.3b keeps free cash flow negative, so funding execution and any future equity needs remain live watch points. The Commerce Commission draft on cost of capital introduces genuine uncertainty over future returns on the expanded asset base. Traffic and revenue are holding up, yet the combination of margin compression, higher non cash charges and regulatory risk shows several key bear milestones are being met rather than disproved.
